_readme: STYLE REGISTRY (Pass 8): category -> the HUMAN-APPROVED reference asset + palette constraints from its governing brief. No entry => npm run art:batch REFUSES the category. Locks are created by humans only: generate candidates, Casey approves ONE on-device, record it here. TECHNIQUE IS PART OF THE LOCK (Casey ruling, Art Session 2): any technique change (conditioning images, model/mode swap) is a lock AMENDMENT - its own bake-off, Casey approval, same ceremony as a new lock. See docs/art-pipeline.md.

terrain-prop.note: Props are a new asset SHAPE under the SAME approved terrain lock (Casey ruling, Art Session 3) - NOT a separate approval and NOT a technique change. Prop recipe addendum lives in docs/art-pipeline.md.
terrain-prop.referenceRole: verification-target: judged against, never generated from

terrain-sheet.techniqueNote: NO conditioning images on any call (Casey ruling, Art Session 2: the approved lock was created prompt-only - that IS its mechanical definition; style-image conditioning was rejected after the first pnw set leaked the grass palette into snow).
terrain-sheet.recipe: create_tiles_pro, square_topdown, 32px, top-down view, segmentation outline mode, seeds in the lock family; numbered four-variant prompt: 1-4 subtle interchangeable variants of ONE ground, same material and tone; shared style words: pixel art, <biome color words> around <anchor hex from src/world/terrain-placeholder.ts>, saturation per biome family, soft front lighting, crisp texture word (tuft/stalk/needle/facet - never weapon homonyms), no objects, no paths
terrain-sheet.referenceRole: verification-target: candidates are JUDGED against this strip (tone, density, readability) - it is never fed into a generation call
terrain-sheet.approved: Casey verdict D, Art Session 1 (grass bake-off, 2026-08-01); technique amendment ruled Art Session 2

pixellab.shape: square_topdown, 32px, top-down view, segmentation outline mode

terrain-sheet.prompt: seamless pixel-art ground, vivid natural color around the biome anchor, slightly rich saturation, soft front lighting, crisp tufted texture, interchangeable subtle variants of one ground, no objects, no flowers, no paths
terrain-sheet.palette: anchor the biome color read from src/world/biome-anchors.ts (BIOME_COLORS, indexed by Biome); roughly 10 colors per tile; mean luminance within 20 percent of the anchor luminance (acceptance band, checked before staging)
terrain-sheet.tileSelection: STANDING POLICY (Casey ruling, Art Session 5): base variants are chosen from a run by BAND, never by file order - in the luminance band, texture at or above the run median, then the four with the smallest pairwise mean-colour spread, tie-broken toward texture. Sessions 1-4 took the first four tiles; that was never a ruling and their approved art stays approved. See docs/art-pipeline.md.

terrain-water.amendment: WATER TECHNIQUE AMENDMENT (Casey verdict, Art Session 5 bake-off on OCEAN). Animated water is a TECHNIQUE EXTENSION of the terrain lock, not a new lock: the same create_tiles_pro recipe, prompt-only, at the same shape and outline mode. What is new is that ONE run is prompted as a numbered travelling-ripple CYCLE, and the three anim cells are selected from that run rather than drawn separately.
terrain-water.recipe: create_tiles_pro, square_topdown, 32px, top-down view, segmentation outline mode. ONE run per water biome, prompted as four numbered phases of a single continuous ripple cycle (crests shifted a step further each time, the fourth about to return to the first), plus the shared terrain style words and the biome anchor read from source. From the run: A2-A4 are the 3-SUBSET whose three pairwise deltas all sit inside the temporal band with the smallest spread between them (a 3-cycle visits all three pairs whatever order it plays, so the choice is a subset, not an ordering); base-0 is the remaining tile nearest that triple's centroid, because base-0 is BOTH the fringe source and the stream-in frame; base-1..3 follow the standing tile-selection policy.
terrain-water.cycler: THE SHEET SERVES THE SHIPPED RENDERER, NOT THE CONTRACT DOC'S ASSUMPTION. src/world/terrain-visuals.ts cycles THREE frames - anim-2, anim-3, anim-4, wrapping anim-4 back to anim-2 - at 450 ms (WATER_ANIM_MS), one global phase written to every water tile on the same tick. base-0..3 are painted at chunk build and overwritten within 450 ms, so they are a stream-in flash only. The 17 fringe cells NEVER animate. A four-frame cycle or animated fringes would be renderer changes and are their own amendment territory.
terrain-water.bands: Derived from the ten shipped sheets, not invented. D = mean per-pixel euclidean RGB distance; D_var = 13.24 = the mean pairwise distance between a shipped sheet's four base variants, i.e. the game's own accepted difference between two draws of one biome. COHERENCE every step <= 0.50*D_var (6.62). LIVENESS every step >= 0.10*D_var (1.32). LOOP the wrap step anim-4 -> anim-2 inside the coherence band AND <= 1.5x the largest forward step. FRINGE COHERENCE D(base-0, A_k) <= D_var, because the coastline is a static ring cut from base-0 around moving water. SEAM seamIndex = wrap boundary / LARGEST interior boundary, per frame, both axes, <= 8.693 (the worst value on approved art), advisory above 1.347 (the typical value). Plus the standing spatial bands per frame.
terrain-water.rejected: animate_image / animate-with-text-v3 (candidate C3) FAILED and is not the technique. Its loop pin is exact (f6 vs f0 = 0.00), but it REDRAWS rather than evolves: consecutive deltas 0.12, 22.76, 15.80, 24.60, 11.40, 13.20, and NO three-frame subset of the generated cycle fits the coherence band at all. Mechanical derivation (C1) passed every band and remains a viable control if a future water biome cannot be generated cleanly.
terrain-water.referenceRole: verification-target: candidates are JUDGED against this sheet, never fed into a generation call
terrain-water.approved: Casey verdict C2, Art Session 5 (ocean bake-off, three candidates, judged on the animated coastline preview)
